definitionEn: the place where planes take off and land
example: We arrived at the airport two hours early.

definitionEn: a journey by plane
example: The flight to London takes two hours.

definitionEn: a person travelling in a plane, train, bus or car
example: Every passenger must show a passport.

definitionEn: an official document that lets you travel to another country
example: My passport expires next year.

definitionEn: a stamp or document that allows you to enter a country
example: You need a visa to visit that country.

definitionEn: the line between two countries
example: We crossed the border by bus.

definitionEn: the place at an airport or border where bags are checked
example: Go through customs after you collect your bags.

definitionEn: when staff search you and your bags before a flight
example: Take off your belt at the security check.

definitionEn: the place where an officer checks your passport
example: The queue at passport control was long.

definitionEn: a large building at an airport for passengers
example: Our flight leaves from terminal two.

definitionEn: the waiting area after security, before you board
example: We sat in the departure lounge and read.

definitionEn: the place where you collect suitcases after a flight
example: Baggage reclaim is downstairs.

definitionEn: a small bag you take into the cabin
example: Hand luggage must fit under the seat.

definitionEn: bags that the airline cannot find
example: We reported lost luggage at the desk.

definitionEn: the long strip where planes take off and land
example: The plane waited on the runway for ten minutes.

definitionEn: a flight that does not stop in another city
example: There is no direct flight from Rzeszów to Dublin.

definitionEn: a short stay in a city between two flights
example: We have a two-hour stopover in Frankfurt.

definitionEn: the staff who look after passengers on a plane
example: The cabin crew showed us the emergency exits.

definitionEn: a belt that holds you in your seat
example: Fasten your seat belt before take-off.

definitionEn: sudden movement of a plane caused by air
example: There was light turbulence over the mountains.

definitionEn: happening later than planned
example: The 8.15 train is delayed by twenty minutes.

definitionEn: a building where trains stop for passengers
example: Meet me at the railway station at five.

definitionEn: a building where coaches and buses start and finish
example: The bus station is next to the shopping centre.

definitionEn: a place at the side of the road where a bus stops
example: Wait at the bus stop opposite the school.

definitionEn: to get on a bus in time
example: If we run, we can catch a bus at ten past.

definitionEn: to arrive too late to get on a train
example: Hurry or you will miss the train.

definitionEn: to leave one train and get on another
example: You have to change trains in Poznań.

definitionEn: to enter a bus, train or plane
example: Get on the tram at the next stop.

definitionEn: to leave a bus, train or plane
example: Get off at the third stop.

definitionEn: to start a journey
example: We set off at six in the morning.

definitionEn: to collect a person in a car
example: Dad will pick up us from the airport.

definitionEn: to take a person somewhere in a car and leave them
example: Can you drop off me at the station?

definitionEn: to pay to use a car for a short time
example: We will hire a car at the airport.

definitionEn: the official card that allows you to drive
example: You need a driving licence to hire a car.

definitionEn: a wide road for fast traffic between cities
example: The motorway to Kraków is busy on Friday.

definitionEn: a circular road where several roads meet
example: Take the second exit at the roundabout.

definitionEn: red, amber and green lights that control traffic
example: Stop when the traffic lights are red.

definitionEn: the highest speed that is legal on a road
example: The speed limit in town is fifty.

definitionEn: a place where you leave a car
example: The car park next to the station is free.

definitionEn: a place where taxis wait for customers
example: There is a taxi rank outside the hotel.

definitionEn: the money you pay for a bus, train or taxi
example: The bus fare is three zloty.

definitionEn: a card that lets you use local buses and trams for a period
example: A monthly travel card is cheaper than singles.

definitionEn: a ticket you can use many times for a month or year
example: Dad has a season ticket for the train to work.

definitionEn: a night train with beds
example: We took the sleeper from Warsaw to Vienna.

definitionEn: the more expensive, more comfortable seats
example: First class is not worth it on a short trip.

definitionEn: a spoken message over loudspeakers
example: Listen to the announcement about platform changes.

definitionEn: a room where you sit until a train or bus comes
example: It is warmer in the waiting room.

definitionEn: a place at a station where you can leave bags for a few hours
example: Leave heavy bags in left luggage while you explore.

definitionEn: the office that keeps things people have lost
example: I found my umbrella in lost property.

definitionEn: a building where you pay to sleep
example: The hotel is a ten-minute walk from the beach.

definitionEn: cheap shared accommodation, often for young travellers
example: We booked a hostel in the city centre.

definitionEn: cheap rooms for young people, often in bunks
example: The youth hostel is next to the station.

definitionEn: a small house that rents rooms to travellers
example: The guest house includes breakfast.

definitionEn: the desk in a hotel where you check in
example: Ask at reception for a city map.

definitionEn: a hotel room for one person
example: I booked a single room for two nights.

definitionEn: a hotel room with one large bed for two people
example: A double room is cheaper than two singles.

definitionEn: a hotel room with two separate beds
example: The twins wanted a twin room.

definitionEn: to pay and leave a hotel
example: We must check out by eleven.

definitionEn: with no free rooms left
example: Every hotel is fully booked in August.

definitionEn: food brought to your hotel room
example: Room service is expensive after midnight.

definitionEn: a system that cools a room
example: Turn on the air conditioning — it is thirty degrees.

definitionEn: a window that looks out over the sea
example: We paid extra for a sea view.

definitionEn: a person who visits a place for pleasure
example: This street is full of tourist shops.

definitionEn: a person who shows visitors around a place
example: The tour guide spoke slowly in English.

definitionEn: a visit to a place with someone who explains it
example: The guided tour of the castle lasts an hour.

definitionEn: a short trip for pleasure, often in a group
example: The hotel offers an excursion to the mountains.

definitionEn: a journey there and back on the same day
example: We went on a day trip to the salt mine.

definitionEn: a short holiday in a city, often a weekend
example: A city break in Prague is cheap by train.

definitionEn: a holiday on a large ship that visits several ports
example: Grandma went on a cruise around the Mediterranean.

definitionEn: a place on the coast where boats stay safely
example: Fishing boats fill the harbour in the morning.

definitionEn: the land next to the sea
example: We drove along the coast to Gdańsk.

definitionEn: a place by the sea where people go on holiday
example: Children love the seaside in summer.

definitionEn: sand or stones next to the sea
example: The beach is crowded in July.

definitionEn: to sit or lie in the sun to get a tan
example: Do not sunbathe between twelve and three.

definitionEn: cream that protects your skin from the sun
example: Put on sunscreen before you go to the beach.

definitionEn: a shelter made of cloth that you sleep in outdoors
example: We put up the tent before it got dark.

definitionEn: a warm bag you sleep in when you camp
example: Bring a thick sleeping bag — nights are cold.

definitionEn: a long walk in the countryside or mountains
example: The hike to the lake takes three hours.

definitionEn: a path for walkers in the hills or forest
example: Follow the red trail to the viewpoint.

definitionEn: a sign that shows the way and the distance
example: The signpost says the village is two kilometres away.

definitionEn: a drawing of an area that shows roads and places
example: I cannot read this map without my glasses.

definitionEn: to ask someone how to get to a place
example: If you get lost, ask the way at a shop.

definitionEn: to continue in the same direction
example: Go straight on until you see the church.

definitionEn: to change direction to the left
example: Turn left after the bridge.

definitionEn: to change direction to the right
example: Turn right at the traffic lights.

definitionEn: money you pay so a company helps if you get ill or lose bags abroad
example: Buy travel insurance before you go abroad.

definitionEn: the money used in a country
example: The currency in Britain is the pound.

definitionEn: how much one currency is worth in another
example: The exchange rate is better at the bank.

definitionEn: a small book of useful sentences in another language
example: A phrasebook helped us order food.

definitionEn: a thin booklet with photos of holidays or places
example: Pick up a brochure at tourist information.

definitionEn: an office that gives maps and advice to visitors
example: Tourist information is in the old town square.

definitionEn: a list of places you will visit and when
example: The itinerary includes two museums and a park.

definitionPl: jet lag, rozstrój po zmianie strefy
definitionEn: tiredness after a long flight across time zones
example: Jet lag made me sleepy at lunchtime.

definitionEn: in or to another country
example: Have you ever lived abroad?
